report.scene_summary: The video shows a warehouse environment with tall racking on the left and open floor space on the right. Pedestrians and wheeled vehicles (forklifts) are present. The camera is static. Several zones have been identified, some containing potential blind spots due to obstructions.

findings.title: Obstructed view at cross-aisle intersection
findings.location: Center of the main aisle where it intersects with the cross-aisle leading to the back wall
findings.observation: A tall stack of palletized boxes on the right side of the main aisle (Z01) blocks the line of sight for a wheeled vehicle traveling down the main aisle from seeing a pedestrian or another vehicle entering from the cross-aisle. Pedestrians are observed walking near this intersection at sampled times (E007, E008).
findings.risk_interpretation: A wheeled vehicle driver traveling down the main aisle cannot see a pedestrian or another vehicle entering from the cross-aisle until it is too late to stop, creating a high risk of collision.
findings.applicability_reason: The obstruction prevents the driver from having a clear view of the path of travel and the cross-aisle intersection.
unknowns: Wheeled vehicle speed at the intersection
Horn usage by wheeled vehicle operators
recommended_actions: Install a convex mirror at the corner of the cross-aisle to provide a view of the main aisle.
Mark a stop line at the intersection and require a horn signal before proceeding.
Reduce speed in the main aisle near the intersection.
Relocate the stacked pallets to improve visibility.

findings.title: Pedestrian walking in vehicle travel lane
findings.location: Right side of the main aisle, near the stacked pallets and wheeled vehicle
findings.observation: A pedestrian in a yellow vest is observed walking within the yellow-lined vehicle travel lane (Z02, Z06) at sampled times (E005, E007, E008, E009, E010, E011). A wheeled vehicle is also present in this lane.
findings.risk_interpretation: A pedestrian walking in a designated vehicle lane is at risk of being struck by a wheeled vehicle or other moving equipment.
findings.applicability_reason: The pedestrian is in an area where mechanical handling equipment is used, and the lane is not clearly separated or marked for pedestrian use.
recommended_actions: Enforce a policy requiring pedestrians to use designated walkways.
Install physical barriers or guardrails to separate pedestrian and vehicle traffic.
Improve visibility of pedestrian walkway markings.
Increase supervision and safety training for both pedestrians and wheeled vehicle operators.

findings.title: Obstructed view at end of rack row
findings.location: Left end of the near rack row (Z03, Z04, Z05) and the end of the rack row further down (Z10)
findings.observation: The tall rack structures and stacked goods at the ends of the aisle (Z03, Z04, Z05, Z10) create blind spots where a pedestrian or wheeled vehicle could emerge from the end of the aisle without being seen by someone in the main aisle. Pedestrians are seen near these areas at sampled times (E016, E017, E019, E031).
findings.risk_interpretation: A pedestrian or wheeled vehicle emerging from the end of an aisle may not be visible to a wheeled vehicle driver or another pedestrian until they are directly in the path of travel, increasing the risk of a collision.
findings.applicability_reason: The racks and goods obstruct the view at the aisle ends, which are locations where vision is obstructed.
unknowns: Wheeled vehicle speed at the aisle ends
Horn usage by wheeled vehicle operators
recommended_actions: Install convex mirrors at the ends of the aisles to provide a view of the main aisle.
Mark stop lines at the aisle ends and require a horn signal before exiting.
Reduce speed in the main aisle near the aisle ends.
Consider using aisle-end guards or barriers to prevent wheeled vehicles from entering the main aisle at these points.
